title: Xanthe and the Cellar
premise: When Ulyana Eastwick returns to the village of Hollowmere to bury his twin sister Xanthe, he insists the body in the coffin isn't hers—despite everyone's gentle assurances and his own fading memories of which twin survived a childhood accident in the family cellar. The village's dead bell begins ringing at dusk each night, counting down, and Ulyana realizes the thing wearing Xanthe's face in the coffin was never interred at all: it walks, and it has been keeping the count that keeps the village fed to something below. To save what's left of his family, Ulyana must descend into the cellar, learn the truth of which twin died decades ago, and take his sister's place at the count—trading his name, his memory, and his survival for theirs.
about_author: Casper Sandoval is the pen name of a former parish archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing funeral registers in remote European villages before turning to fiction. His work draws on the ledgers he was never supposed to read, and he has never confirmed whether Hollowmere appears on any map.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sister
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. Ulyana arrives in Hollowmere for the burial and refuses to view the body, insisting his twin Xanthe is alive—though he cannot say how he knows. His mother weeps with relief or grief; even Ulyana can't tell. The emotional beat is denial sharpening into dread when the melted bell rings at dusk and every villager bows their head as if they'd been waiting for it.

chapters.title: What the Registers Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. Digging through the church archives, Ulyana finds his own death recorded in 1998—and Xanthe's signature renewing an annual 'count' ever since. The villagers grow hostile as the bell rings closer together each night. The beat is loyalty fracturing against truth: everyone he loves has been protecting him from a bargain made in his name.

chapters.title: The Count Below
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. The bell rings continuously; the village doors begin opening on their own. Ulyana descends into the flooded cellar and meets the thing that has worn his sister's shape for twenty-five years—not a monster but a caretaker, starving because the count lapsed when 'Xanthe' died. Climax: Ulyana must choose between running with his mother or taking up the count himself.

chapters.title: Bellringer
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana, thinning into second person as his memory erodes. He accepts the bargain: the village wakes safe, his mother boards a bus she doesn't remember boarding, and something patient climbs out of the coffin wearing his face. Resolution lands on the price of survival—the final line reveals a new archivist arriving in Hollowmere, asking about a bell that shouldn't exist.
